correctness.rationale: The normalized Gibbs state has tangent \(-h/d\) at the maximally mixed state, with h the centered Hamiltonian. Applying the entropy Hessian \(S(I/n+\varepsilon X)=\log n-(n\varepsilon^2/2)\operatorname{Tr}(X^2)+O(\varepsilon^3)\) to the joint state and both marginals yields the difference of three squared Hilbert--Schmidt norms. Orthogonally decomposing h into A-only, B-only, and interaction components leaves exactly \(\operatorname{Tr}(H_{\mathrm{int}}^2)/d\). Vanishing interaction is equivalent to a commuting local-plus-scalar decomposition and hence exact Gibbs factorization. Pauli orthogonality gives the crossing-string form. For disjoint Ising bonds the state factorizes over bonds and the exact one-bond mutual information is \(x\tanh x-\log\cosh x\), giving the claimed sharpness. The inspected verifier independently checks the projection algebra, a noncommuting two-qubit numerical Hessian, the Pauli form, and the Ising formula.

value.rationale: The exact coefficient answers a natural question left behind by a current nonperturbative area-law result: which Hamiltonian components contribute at the first nonzero high-temperature order. It cleanly removes all bulk-only directions, gives a directly computable Pauli formula, and supplies an exact family saturating both quadratic temperature dependence and linear boundary scaling. This is a motivated structural refinement rather than an arbitrary Taylor coefficient.
residual_risks: The coefficient alone does not control higher-order volume dependence at fixed positive temperature.

final_claim: For every finite-dimensional bipartite Hamiltonian, the Gibbs mutual information has the infinite-temperature expansion \(I(A:B)_{\rho_\beta}=\beta^2\operatorname{Tr}(H_{\mathrm{int}}^2)/(2d)+O(\beta^3)\), where \(H_{\mathrm{int}}\) is the Hilbert--Schmidt projection orthogonal to all one-sided Hamiltonians. The coefficient vanishes exactly for local-plus-scalar Hamiltonians, in which case the Gibbs state factorizes at every temperature. For qubit Pauli expansions it is one half the sum of squared crossing coefficients, and disjoint Ising bonds give an exact witness showing simultaneous sharpness of quadratic temperature order and linear boundary scaling.
limitations: Finite-dimensional systems only; the expansion is local at \(\beta=0\) for each fixed Hamiltonian.
No finite-temperature area-law bound, thermodynamic-limit interchange, or optimal nonperturbative constant is claimed.
